subject: SLO & traffic envelope: latency targets and peak token windows
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.s@atlashealth.io>, Rahul Menon <rahul@atlashealth.io>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO & traffic envelope: latency targets and peak token windows

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap from our side + the open items we discussed so engineering can start a sizing pass. Short version at top, full notes below.

TL;DR:
- Target p50/p95 generation latency goal: 80ms / 250ms (application goal).
- Expected steady-state: ~45 QPS with ~1.2k tokens/sec average across requests.
- Two predictable peaks per day (~09:00 and ~17:00 ET) where traffic can jump ~3x for 3-8 minutes.
- Streaming: yes for patient-facing assistant (partial tokens streamed back).

Notes from the call:
- Workload mix: 70% short responses (<200 tokens), 25% medium (200–800), 5% long (>800).
- Typical request pattern: client opens socket, initial prompt -> back-and-forth streaming for follow-ups (average 2.1 rounds).
- Concurrency: front-end holds ~30 concurrent websockets during steady-state; peaks up to ~90 concurrent sockets during burst windows.

Open asks (would appreciate answers by EOD Tue so we can size):
1) Can you confirm the 3x peak multiplier and the typical duration you see for each peak window (we noted 3–8 minutes)?
2) Are any requests likely to hit >2k tokens in a single prompt/response cycle (you said ~5% long — can you quantify)?
3) Any hard latency SLAs to preserve for streaming (p50/p95 for first token / subsequent tokens)?
4) If you have a CSV snapshot of recent traffic (timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, connection_id) please attach — our engineer will ingest it for a realistic run.

Attachments: redwood_followup_questions.xlsx (form with fields we mentioned)

Next steps from our side:
- Once we get the snapshot and answers above, Dylan (cc'd later) will run a throughput sizing and propose a dedicated vs hosted configuration and expected cost bands.
- We'll propose a canary rollout plan for streaming to meet latency SLOs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.s@atlashealth.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 18:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLO & traffic envelope: latency targets and peak token windows

Monica — thanks for the thorough write-up. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Can you confirm the 3x peak multiplier and the typical duration you see for each peak window (we noted 3–8 minutes)?
Yes, 3x is a good approximation for our two daily peaks. We pulled a 2-week sample; typical peak durations are 4–6 minutes, sometimes up to 10 minutes if a promotional banner drives traffic.

> 2) Are any requests likely to hit >2k tokens in a single prompt/response cycle (you said ~5% long — can you quantify)?
Long requests are ~4–6% of total. Of those, only ~10% exceed 2k tokens (so ~0.4–0.6% of all requests). Most long sessions are multi-turn rather than single-shot giant prompts.

> 3) Any hard latency SLAs to preserve for streaming (p50/p95 for first token / subsequent tokens)?
We don't have contractual SLA yet, but product requires UX targets: first token p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms; subsequent token p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms. If you can size for better (your 80/250 suggestion) we'd be happy.

> 4) If you have a CSV snapshot of recent traffic...
Attaching a 48-hour export as requested: atlas_workload_snapshot.csv (CSV columns: ts_iso, connection_id, direction, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms). The file is scrubbed for PHI.

We also confirmed that ~18% of requests are from mobile clients (higher latency variance). We expect growth of ~20% MoM over next quarter.

Happy to jump on a short follow-up after Dylan's sizing.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Integrations | Atlas Health
priya.s@atlashealth.io

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.s@atlashealth.io>, Rahul Menon <rahul@atlashealth.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO & traffic envelope: latency targets and peak token windows

Thanks Priya — the snapshot is perfect and the clarifications help. Looping in Dylan from our Performance team to run the sizing pass. Dylan — details below and attached CSV. Key points for sizing:
- Steady-state: 45 QPS, ~1.2k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Bursts: ~3x traffic for 4–6 minutes, up to 10 minutes.
- Streaming behavior: websocket partial token streaming (first token latency requirement noted).
- Token distribution: 70/25/5 split, ~0.5% requests >2k tokens.

Dylan — can you run two scenarios and share back by EOD Thu?
A) Hosted minimal: use our hosted-cpu/GPU mix to satisfy 80/250 p50/p95. Provide expected cost per 100k requests and required upper concurrency.
B) Dedicated recommendation: GPUs required, expected reserved capacity sizing for 20% growth buffer + canary plan for streaming.

Also please highlight any fallback model choices if we can't meet streaming p95 with the largest model (e.g., prefer quantized variant with shorter context for streaming).

Attachments: atlas_workload_snapshot.csv

Thanks both — we'll schedule a short 30-min sync once the sizing runs are ready.

Best,
Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Appreciate the quick loop-in, Monica — thanks Dylan in advance. Two quick clarifications before you run numbers: 
1) For the burst windows, can you model both a hard 3x and a soft 4x scenario (4x happens during marketing spikes).
2) If you provide an initial cost band, can you include an estimate for optional KV-prefix caching (we expect a lot of repeated prefixes in the short responses).

We'll be available for the 30-min sync Thu or Fri depending on your availability.

—Priya
